From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call next steps: schedule deep-dive & sizing for BrightBank

Hi Kyle — great chat earlier today, thanks for walking us through BrightBank's conversational fraud-detection use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: run a dedicated capacity sizing call to validate throughput and latency targets and determine pool sizing for a staged rollout.
- Inputs we ideally need before the call: representative request QPS, typical and peak sequence lengths (token distribution), concurrency targets, and any SLA windows that matter. (I attached a brief profile sheet you can fill — BrightBank_Inference_Profile.xlsx)
- Proposed meeting: 60-minute technical deep-dive + sizing with Redwood engineering (we'll bring Ben for runtime/ops details).

Suggested windows (PST):
- Wed 21 Sep, 10:00–11:00
- Thu 22 Sep, 14:00–15:00
- Fri 23 Sep, 09:00–10:00

If none of those work, send a couple alternatives and we’ll adapt. Also looping Ben for ops-level notes; Naomi from CS will join the kickoff if the timeline looks like late September.

Next step ask: can you share a rough QPS target and token-length percentile (p50/p95) ahead of the call? Even ballpark numbers help us prepare an accurate pool estimate.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

— Soojin

Thanks Soojin — appreciated the clear recap. We want to get this on calendar. High-level numbers from our infra team:

- Steady-state QPS: ~40 requests/sec (chat endpoint, single-turn)
- Peak QPS observed (event-driven spikes): up to ~220 r/s for ~10–15 minute bursts
- Typical prompt length: 120 tokens (p50), 780 tokens (p95) including system instructions and user message
- Desired latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for user-facing inference (low-latency path preferred)

Either Wed 21 10:00 or Thu 22 14:00 works for us — prefer Wed if possible. I’ll ask infra@brightbank.com to fill the attached profile and forward any logs we can share.

Kyle
Kyle Torres
Sr. Engineering Manager — Platforms, BrightBank

Prep notes for the call (we'll prepare these items on our side):
- Redwood will run a short pre-call simulation using your p50/p95 token shapes and the QPS numbers you provided to produce a baseline GPU pool estimate (we aim to share a 1-page estimate during the call).
- We'll bring: Ben (runtime/inference ops) and a runtime engineer to discuss kernel/quantization options and fallback policies; Naomi will cover onboarding/training and any long-term monitoring needs.
- Please have someone from infra join who can speak to traffic shaping, burst mitigation, and any compliance constraints (e.g., private deployment requirements).

Action items for you before Wed:
- Fill BrightBank_Inference_Profile.xlsx with sample traffic shapes and a recent 1-hour log snippet if available

Hi all — thanks for the numbers, Kyle. Quick ops note ahead of the call:

Given p95 sequence ~780 tokens and burst up to 220 r/s, we'll likely discuss a hybrid approach: dedicated GPU pool sized for steady-state with burst capacity via autoscale and an optimized low-latency model (quantized + KV cache warm-up) for the critical user path. For the pre-call simulation I can run two scenarios (conservative and aggressive) if Kyle’s team can indicate budget sensitivity (do we prefer lower-latency at higher cost, or a cost-balanced target?).

Naomi — FYI — please prepare the onboarding slide outlining required telemetry and expected ramp cadence.

See you Wed 10am.

— Ben
